bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Advertising revenue dependence and a structurally weak ad market — Advertising revenue declined 10% YoY as the advertising environment remained subdued, hit by softness in FMCG spending and geopolitical uncertainties in the latter part of the year. Advertising is a large, cyclical share of the revenue base and is the primary swing factor in profitability.
- Structural migration of ad spend from linear TV to digital and Q-commerce — The Linear TV industry's revenue declined 9%, with advertising hit by reduced volumes and reallocation of budgets towards Q-Commerce and other digital advertising, while linear subscription revenue fell 8% on shrinking Pay TV households. A large part of Zee's base sits in the shrinking linear pool.
- Content cost and amortisation policy risk — Operating costs were affected by a revision in estimates on the amortisation pattern of movie rights inventory and additional impairment, so content costs were recognised on a more accelerated basis. This drove reported EBITDA well below adjusted EBITDA and shows how sensitive earnings are to content valuation and consumption assumptions.
- Studio / theatrical performance volatility — Other sales and services grew only 2%, with momentum in syndication partially offset by a muted performance in the studio segment - a hit-driven business whose outcomes are inherently unpredictable.
- Regulatory and legal exposure, including a pending SEBI matter — The Directors' Report records that the Company and its KMP have challenged a SEBI order before the appellate authority and that the matter is presently sub-judice. Profitability for the year was also impacted by higher legal costs, making litigation an active earnings drag.
- Execution risk on new growth verticals — Growth depends on scaling recently launched or acquired businesses - sports (including the FIFA rights portfolio and four Unite8 channels), kids, micro-drama and live events - which require upfront investment ahead of monetisation.
- Geopolitical and macro sensitivity — Advertising revenue was explicitly impacted by the Middle East crisis that started in February 2026 and by geopolitical uncertainties in the latter part of the year, and management notes a slow recovery in consumption demand.
- Forward-looking assumptions may not hold — The MD&A cautionary statement warns that forward-looking statements rely on assumptions inherently subject to risks and uncertainties, that there is a significant risk those assumptions and predictions may not prove accurate, and that readers should not place undue reliance on them.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Zee is an asset-light media business, so expansion is footprint, content-rights and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. During FY26 the Company forayed into kids entertainment by launching KidZ on ZEE5 in November 2025, and continued to scale the Bullet micro-drama app. It made strategic investments across emerging segments - kids, sports, live events and micro-drama - and invested Rs 1,160 million in Phantom Digital Effects Limited, a global VFX company, to strengthen AVGC capabilities and enable more immersive content. In sports, it repurposed the Zee Cafe and &Flix channel brands into dedicated sports feeds under the Zee Sports cluster, secured exclusive multi-platform rights to marquee properties including the ILT20 and the Uttar Pradesh Kabaddi League, and expanded into baseball and pickleball leagues. In June 2026 it secured exclusive rights to broadcast, stream and distribute a portfolio of 39 FIFA competitions in India from 2026 to 2034, and launched four sports channels under the Unite8 umbrella alongside rights to Bundesliga and Serie A. Corporate-structure expansion during the year comprised the incorporation of ZBullet Enterprises Limited (June 12, 2025), Rotate OneTouch Limited (June 28, 2025) and ZI-IPR Enterprises Limited (October 1, 2025), and the acquisition of the remaining 10% of Margo Networks Private Limited on December 31, 2025 making it wholly owned. Physical footprint as disclosed in BRSR Section A is 1 plant (a standalone data centre) and 14 offices nationally, plus 8 international offices. Funding intent for further organic and inorganic growth was to be met through a preferential issue of fully convertible warrants to promoter group entities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Media & Entertainment sector grew 9% in 2025, led by digital media which expanded 30% and became the largest segment of the industry
- Digital advertising grew 26% to Rs 947 billion on the continued shift of ad spend from traditional media, Q-Commerce traction and rising SME/long-tail contribution; digital subscription revenues rose 60% to Rs 163 billion on paywalled premium content, OTT growth and better music-streaming monetisation
- Linear TV industry revenue declined 9% - advertising hit by lower ad volumes, budget reallocation to Q-Commerce and digital, the real-money-gaming ban affecting sports advertising, and an FMCG ad-spend slowdown; subscription revenue fell 8% on Pay TV household losses, partially offset by price increases
- Zee's own advertising revenue was pressured by slow recovery in consumption demand among FMCG companies, the shift of ad spend to digital and Q-commerce, and the Middle East crisis from February 2026; the Company nonetheless saw gradual sequential recovery supported by improved network share and enhanced content
- Subscription growth is led by the digital business, aided by the success of the seven-language pricing packs and an improved subscriber base, with NTO 3.0 implementation providing partial inflation-aligned support to linear subscription revenue
- Operating costs were affected by a revision in the amortisation pattern of movie rights inventory and additional impairment, so content costs were recognised on a more accelerated basis in line with evolving content consumption trends and lower recent content capitalisation
- Cost optimisation across programming, manpower and overheads kept total operating expenses largely stable, partially offset by strategic investment in digital growth, content creation and new initiatives
- Filmed entertainment is projected to grow at a 7% CAGR to Rs 253 billion by 2028, driven by cinema infrastructure in under-served geographies, evolving release windows and diverse storytelling formats; domestic theatrical is expected to remain the primary profitability anchor with international distribution maturing steadily
- The organised live events market is projected to reach nearly Rs 196 billion by 2028 (10% CAGR), supported by demand for premium experiences, year-round event calendars and broader audience participation - a growth runway management identifies for Z Live
- India's sports segment revenues expanded from Rs 196 billion to Rs 223 billion in 2025, propelled by a 20% surge in media spend; cricket dominates with 95% of media rights and 89% of industry revenues, framing the opportunity in non-cricket franchises
- Connected TV households, smartphone penetration and higher consumption of regional and short-form content are structural tailwinds for the digital segment
- Management states that continued investments in digital, content innovation and omnichannel monetisation, coupled with a lean cost structure, position the Company to capitalise on an improving macro environment

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Media & Entertainment sector grew 9% in 2025, led by digital media which expanded 30% and became the largest segment of the industry
- Digital advertising grew 26% to Rs 947 billion on the continued shift of ad spend from traditional media, Q-Commerce traction and rising SME/long-tail contribution; digital subscription revenues rose 60% to Rs 163 billion on paywalled premium content, OTT growth and better music-streaming monetisation
- Linear TV industry revenue declined 9% - advertising hit by lower ad volumes, budget reallocation to Q-Commerce and digital, the real-money-gaming ban affecting sports advertising, and an FMCG ad-spend slowdown; subscription revenue fell 8% on Pay TV household losses, partially offset by price increases
- Zee's own advertising revenue was pressured by slow recovery in consumption demand among FMCG companies, the shift of ad spend to digital and Q-commerce, and the Middle East crisis from February 2026; the Company nonetheless saw gradual sequential recovery supported by improved network share and enhanced content
- Subscription growth is led by the digital business, aided by the success of the seven-language pricing packs and an improved subscriber base, with NTO 3.0 implementation providing partial inflation-aligned support to linear subscription revenue
- Operating costs were affected by a revision in the amortisation pattern of movie rights inventory and additional impairment, so content costs were recognised on a more accelerated basis in line with evolving content consumption trends and lower recent content capitalisation
- Cost optimisation across programming, manpower and overheads kept total operating expenses largely stable, partially offset by strategic investment in digital growth, content creation and new initiatives
- Filmed entertainment is projected to grow at a 7% CAGR to Rs 253 billion by 2028, driven by cinema infrastructure in under-served geographies, evolving release windows and diverse storytelling formats; domestic theatrical is expected to remain the primary profitability anchor with international distribution maturing steadily
- The organised live events market is projected to reach nearly Rs 196 billion by 2028 (10% CAGR), supported by demand for premium experiences, year-round event calendars and broader audience participation - a growth runway management identifies for Z Live
- India's sports segment revenues expanded from Rs 196 billion to Rs 223 billion in 2025, propelled by a 20% surge in media spend; cricket dominates with 95% of media rights and 89% of industry revenues, framing the opportunity in non-cricket franchises
- Connected TV households, smartphone penetration and higher consumption of regional and short-form content are structural tailwinds for the digital segment
- Management states that continued investments in digital, content innovation and omnichannel monetisation, coupled with a lean cost structure, position the Company to capitalise on an improving macro environment

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% in Q4; pressured by legal expenses and ad slowdown. Employee costs optimized (-16% Q4, -9% FY26) via manpower rationalization to target 9% of revenue ratio. Marketing spend up 44% Q4 deemed essential for new business launches and daily consumption retention.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on strengthening liquidity (INR 27.6B cash/investments); selective M&A for capability building (VFX, Live); open to strategic partnerships or demerger for Zee Music if valuation attractive; no large-scale buybacks/dividends highlighted amidst reinvestment phase.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Zee is an asset-light media business, so expansion is footprint, content-rights and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. During FY26 the Company forayed into kids entertainment by launching KidZ on ZEE5 in November 2025, and continued to scale the Bullet micro-drama app. It made strategic investments across emerging segments - kids, sports, live events and micro-drama - and invested Rs 1,160 million in Phantom Digital Effects Limited, a global VFX company, to strengthen AVGC capabilities and enable more immersive content. In sports, it repurposed the Zee Cafe and &Flix channel brands into dedicated sports feeds under the Zee Sports cluster, secured exclusive multi-platform rights to marquee properties including the ILT20 and the Uttar Pradesh Kabaddi League, and expanded into baseball and pickleball leagues. In June 2026 it secured exclusive rights to broadcast, stream and distribute a portfolio of 39 FIFA competitions in India from 2026 to 2034, and launched four sports channels under the Unite8 umbrella alongside rights to Bundesliga and Serie A. Corporate-structure expansion during the year comprised the incorporation of ZBullet Enterprises Limited (June 12, 2025), Rotate OneTouch Limited (June 28, 2025) and ZI-IPR Enterprises Limited (October 1, 2025), and the acquisition of the remaining 10% of Margo Networks Private Limited on December 31, 2025 making it wholly owned. Physical footprint as disclosed in BRSR Section A is 1 plant (a standalone data centre) and 14 offices nationally, plus 8 international offices. Funding intent for further organic and inorganic growth was to be met through a preferential issue of fully convertible warrants to promoter group entities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale of viewership - 852 million viewers tuned into the Z network during the year, with the gap to the leading network at only 2% despite operating nearly half the number of channels
- Linear viewership share reached a six-year high of 17.4% in FY26, up 60 basis points
- Omni-channel reach - monthly unique reach has crossed 800 million across platforms
- International broadcasting footprint of over 40 dedicated channels and more than 75 pass-through channels across over 120 countries, a model the Company describes itself as a pioneer in
- Music library moat - Zee Music Company has ~176 million YouTube subscribers in India and a catalogue of over 20,000 songs across more than 20 languages, the second-most-listened-to Indian music label
- Integrated film vertical combining production, distribution and cross-platform promotion; Zee Studios has a portfolio of over 150 films and global theatrical distribution capability
- ZEE5 digital business achieved EBITDA breakeven and turned profitable on a comparable basis in FY26, its first year of positive digital EBITDA
- Content-security controls including Multi-Key Digital Rights Management and automated anti-piracy tooling on ZEE5
- Ranked among the top 5% in the Media, Movies and Entertainment sector globally in the S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) 2025

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Prolonged Middle East/West Asia conflict suppressing ad budgets; inflationary pressure reducing consumer discretionary spend on subscriptions; intense competition in OTT and Music segments; execution risk in new verticals (Live, VFX, Micro-drama).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly linked the 80bps market share gain to a 13-16 week revenue conversion lag, implying Q1/Q2 FY27 could see disproportionate ad upside if macro stabilizes; the accelerated amortization is a non-cash accounting alignment to digital viewing trends, artificially depressing current PAT while cleaning up future P&L.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Contradiction — Mar'26 cash] The condensed balance sheet shows "Cash and other investments" of Rs 27,595 Mn at Mar'26 and Rs 22,109 Mn at Jun'26, while the treasury-detail footnote states "The cash & treasury investments as of Mar'26 stood at Rs 22,109 Mn, including Mutual Fund of Rs 11,800 Mn, Bank FDs of Rs 5,944 Mn and Cash balance and other treasury investments of Rs 4,364 Mn." Both readings are quoted as-is; the deck does not reconcile them.
- [Demand shock] The deck states "Q1 FY27 Middle East Crisis Impacted Advertising Revenue; Partially offset by FIFA performance" and that "Domestic advertising revenue impacted due to Middle East Crisis & Cricket in Q1".
- [International] International revenue break-up for Q1 FY27 is given as Advertising Rs 460 Mn, Subscription Rs 1,035 Mn, Other Sales & Services Rs 155 Mn, with "Overall revenue down 11% YoY".
- [Accounting change] Several figures carry a footnote referring to "the change in estimates of movie rights inventory amortisation pattern" and "additional impairment", which the deck says are included in Q4 FY26 reported numbers and excluded from the adjusted ones.
- [Filing context] The document bundles a BSE/NSE letter dated August 10, 2026 giving notice that the audio recording of the Q1 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) conference call is available on the company website.
